citations.quote: Efficacy of loncastuximab tesirine is based on the results from ADCT-402-201, an open-label, multicenter, single-arm trial which included 145 adult patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma after at least 2 prior systemic regimens.
Of the 145 patients enrolled, the median age was 66 years (range 23 to 94), 59% male, and 94% had an ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
The median number of prior therapies was 3 (range 2 to 7), 63% with refractory disease, 17% with prior stem cell transplant, and 9% with prior chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy.

target_moa.text: CD19-directed antibody-drug conjugate; the monoclonal antibody binds human CD19, is internalized, and releases the pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) dimer SG3199, a DNA crosslinking agent that forms cytotoxic DNA interstrand crosslinks inducing cell cycle arrest and cell death.

citations.quote: The monoclonal antibody binds to human CD19. The small molecule cytotoxin, PBD dimer (SG3199), is a DNA crosslinking agent conjugated to the antibody via a protease-cleavable

Upon binding CD19, loncastuximab tesirine is internalized and the linker is cleaved by lysosomal proteases to enable release of the PBD dimer which then binds to the DNA minor groove and forms highly cytotoxic DNA interstrand crosslinks, subsequently inducing cell cycle arrest and cell death.

modality.text: ADC (antibody-drug conjugate): CD19-directed monoclonal antibody conjugated to the PBD dimer SG3199

citations.quote: Loncastuximab tesirine is an antibody drug conjugate consisting of a CD19-targeted monoclonal antibody bound to the DNA crosslinking pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) dimer, cytotoxic drug, SG3199, via a protease-cleavable valine-alanine linker.

key_safety.text: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions including lab abnormalities: thrombocytopenia, increased gamma-glutamyltransferase, neutropenia, anemia, hyperglycemia, transaminase elevation, fatigue, hypoalbuminemia, rash, edema, nausea, and musculoskeletal pain. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia in 32%, thrombocytopenia in 20%, anemia in 12%. Serious adverse reactions in 28%; fatal adverse reactions in 1% due to infection.

citations.quote: In this pooled safety population of 215 patients, the most common (>20%) adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, were thrombocytopenia, increased gamma-glutamyltransferase, neutropenia, anemia, hyperglycemia, transaminase elevation, fatigue, hypoalbuminemia, rash, edema, nausea, and musculoskeletal pain.
Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 32%, thrombocytopenia in 20%, and anemia in 12% of patients.

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 28% of patients receiving ZYNLONTA. The most common serious adverse reactions that occurred in \ge 2\% receiving ZYNLONTA were febrile neutropenia, pneumonia, edema, pleural effusion, and sepsis. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1%, due to infection.
